items.q: What should you remember about **Mumbling = small mouth movements**?
items.a: **unclear speech is usually** a physical articulation problem, not just "thinking too fast.".

items.q: What should you remember about **Over-articulation works immediately**?
items.a: **exaggerating pronunciation in the moment produces** audibly crisp results; it may feel theatrical but that is the point.

items.q: What should you remember about **5 minutes daily with a book**?
items.a: **sustained practice normalizes large mouth** movements; sounding "British" or "trying too hard" is acceptable during training.

items.q: What should you remember about **Volume and energy are part of articulation**?
items.a: **low motor volume undermines** clarity even when syllables are correct.

items.q: What should you remember about **Sentence-level energy**?
items.a: **most speakers lose energy mid-sentence** (crackly vocal fry); maintain the same vitality from first word to last.

items.q: What should you remember about **Count-to-10 equal-energy drill**?
items.a: **each number at identical** volume/energy trains consistent vocal presence before full sentences.

items.q: What should you remember about **Nasality vs crispness**?
items.a: **nasal tone ("when I talk I sound** like this") is distinct from poor articulation; the demo student had neither after the drill.
